abstract: REDUCED SYSTEMIC IMMUNITY 1(RSI1)/FLOWERING LOCUS D (FLD) is essential for the activation of systemic acquired resistance (SAR). RSI1 functions as a repressor of gene expression by demethylating H3K4me2 and H3K4me3. RSI1 expression is induced both in local and systemic tissues upon pathogen inoculation. However, the mechanism of its induction or its expression regulation upon pathogenesis is not known. Here we show that RSI1 expression in SAR-induced rsi1 mutant plants is higher than WT plants, suggesting self-regulation. Pathogen-induced expression of RSI1 requires the function of GSTT2, a SANT domain-containing protein essential for SAR activation. Co-expression of RSI1 suppresses pRSI1:GUS activity in a transient assay system. Chromatin-immunoprecipitation (ChIP) experiments reveal that RSI1 physically associates near the transcription start site (TSS) of the RSI1 locus and facilitates demethylation of H3K4me2 and H3K4me3 at RSI1 locus. Our data altogether demonstrate that RSI1 negatively regulates its own expression as a possible mechanism of keep the SAR expression at an optimal level.
